boilerplate.general_comments_title: General Comments about the Quantitative Reasoning Section
general_comments: The figures accompanying some of the problems are provided to help solve the problems, but are not necessarily drawn to scale.  Therefore, do not rely on the figures alone to deduce line length, angle size, and so forth.
If a line in a figure appears to be straight, you may assume that it is in fact a straight line.
When a geometric term (side, radius, area, volume, etc.) appears in a problem, it refers to a term whose value is greater than 0, unless stated otherwise.
When \(\sqrt{a}\) (a > 0) appears in a problem, it refers to the positive root of a.
"0" is neither a positive nor a negative number.

clusters.intro:
Study the table below, then answer the five questions that follow.

At the beginning of every year a ranking of the hundred tallest buildings in the world is published.
The table below presents data concerning ten tall buildings, marked with the letters A-J.  For each building the table records the city in which it is located, its height, and its place in the ranking in each of the years 2001, 2002, 2003 and 2004.
Between the publication dates of every two rankings, new buildings that were built are added to the ranking (and do not appear in the table), but existing buildings are not demolished.

Note: Assume that no two buildings have the same height.

Study the graph below, then answer the five questions that follow.

The security team at a certain museum numbers 24 guards.  After they discovered that exactly two guards were born in every month of the year, they decided to divide the work among themselves by means of a lottery based on their birth months.

The lottery wheel, presented in the graph, is divided into twelve identical-sized sectors and is mounted on a wall.  On the wall, around the wheel, the names of the twelve months are written.  Before every week the wheel is spun so that at the end of the spin each sector stops opposite one of the months.
A sector determines for the two guards born in that month their duties in the coming week: how many day shifts and how many night shifts each of them will work, whether they will be members of the alert squad, whether they will be scouts and whether they will be the weekly duty officers (see key).

For example, if the wheel stopped in the position in which it now appears in the graph, the two weekly duty officers are the guards born in the month of August, and the two guards born in September worked 3 day shifts and 2 night shifts each.  Had the wheel stopped so that the guards born in the month of September were the weekly duty officers, then the guards born in the month of August would each work 4 day shifts and would also be members of the alert squad.

questions.stem: Given: 0 < a c < b < 0 Which of the following expressions is necessarily positive?

methods.text: Mark the signs: \(a\) is positive, and \(c<b<0\) makes both \(b\) and \(c\) negative. Two negative factors is an even count, so \(a\cdot b\cdot c\) is positive.

Options (3) and (4) fail for a different reason worth naming: \(b+1\) and \(a-1\) have no determined sign at all. An unknown-sign factor anywhere in a product kills the option outright, before any counting.
Option (2) has \(b^2\), which erases one minus and leaves an odd count — so it is negative. That leaves only (1).
Over the common denominator 30: \(\frac{3+6+10+15}{30} - 1 = \frac{34}{30} - 1 = \frac{4}{30} = \frac{2}{15}\).
The four fractions sum to slightly more than 1, so the answer must be small and positive — which alone rules out nothing here, but does confirm the sign before any arithmetic.

Given:  3 < x < 4

Which of the following values can be the value of x?

methods.text: Square the given range instead of the options: \(9<x^2<16\). Now the question is simply which radicand lands strictly inside, and only 14 does.
\(\sqrt8\) is below 3 and both \(\sqrt{18}\) and \(\sqrt{22}\) are above 4, so all three fall outside the band. Moving the given to meet the options is faster than estimating four square roots.

questions.stem: The regular price of a kg of peanuts is 5 shekels. Two shops are selling peanuts on sale: Shop A sells every 1.2 kg of peanuts for 5 shekels. Shop B sells peanuts at a discount of 20% off the regular price. Uriel wants to buy 6 kg of peanuts in one of the shops. What is the difference (in shekels) between the amount he would pay in shop A and the amount he would pay in shop B?

methods.text: Shop A: 6 kg at 1.2 kg per 5 shekels is 5 lots, costing 25. Shop B: 6 kg at \(5 \times 0.8 = 4\) each, costing 24. The difference is 1.
A's offer is really a discount of \(\frac{1}{6}\) (about 16.7%), which is less than B's 20% — so B is cheaper, and by a single shekel.

In the accompanying figure there are two parallel straight lines, a and b. Straight line c cuts straight lines a and b. Which of the following statements is not necessarily true?
Factory A produces 6a cars in 2 hours. Factory B produces 4a cars in 6 hours. How many cars are produced in factory A and in factory B together in 18a hours?

methods.text: A makes \(3a\) cars an hour, B makes \(\frac{2a}{3}\), so together \(\frac{11a}{3}\). Over \(18a\) hours that is \(66a^2\).
The \(a\) appears in both the rate and the time, so the answer is quadratic in \(a\). Options (1) and (2) cannot be right on the power of \(a\) alone.

questions.stem:
m is an integer greater than 1.
Given:  \(m^{2x} = m \cdot m^{(x^2)}\)

x = ?

methods.text: Same base with \(m>1\), so the exponents match: \(2x = 1+x^2\), which is \((x-1)^2 = 0\), giving \(x=1\).
Substituting \(x=1\) gives \(m^2 = m \cdot m\) at once. With four numeric options, testing beats solving.

Elisheva donated all of her library to three schools.  The ratio of the division was 5:9:11.  She donated 575 books in total.

How many books did the school to which Elisheva donated the largest number of books receive?

methods.text: The parts total \(5+9+11 = 25\), so one part is \(\frac{575}{25} = 23\). The largest share is \(11 \times 23 = 253\).
Ratio questions are division into equal parts. Finding the size of one part first makes every share a single multiplication.

questions.stem:
Given:  \(y = \frac{a \cdot b}{x}\)

a and b are prime numbers, greater than 10 and different from each other.
x and y are two integers greater than 1.

Which of the following statements is true with regard to x and to y?
options: Both of them are necessarily prime.
One of them is necessarily prime, and the other one – not necessarily.
It is possible that x = y.

methods.text: \(xy = ab\) with \(a\) and \(b\) distinct primes above 10. The only ways to split \(ab\) into two factors above 1 are \(a \times b\) — there is nothing else, because \(a\) and \(b\) are prime.
So \(\{x,y\} = \{a,b\}\) and both are prime. They cannot be equal, since \(a \ne b\), and \(x = 2y\) would need one to be twice the other, impossible for two primes above 10.

questions.stem:
Ilana has a sheet of paper in the shape of a triangle as in the figure, and stickers in the shape of a square each one of which has an area of 1 cm².
She is interested in sticking the stickers on the triangular sheet so that they do not cover one another and do not exceed the boundaries of the sheet, and without cutting any sticker (she sticks all of them on the same side of the sheet).

How many whole stickers, at most, will Ilana be able to stick in this way?

A spacecraft flew from Earth to the moon in a straight line at a constant speed of 100 kph.
The distance between Earth and the moon is about 380,000 km.

Which of the following lengths of time is closest to the length of time that the spacecraft would need in order to reach the moon?
(there are 24 hours in a day and 365 days in a year)

methods.text: \(\frac{380{,}000}{100} = 3800\) hours. Dividing by 24 gives about 158 days.

158 days is roughly five months, so 'half a year' is the nearest option — the others are 30 days, a week and two years, all off by a factor of five or more. Convert to days and stop; there is no need for a precise fraction of a year.
